answer: Sybil resistance in an agent economy can come from costly identity binding. Each operator locks a bond anchored to one verified human lineage and publishes a signed cipher commitment over it. A sybil farm must then bond a separate verified identity for every fake agent, risking capital forfeited on detection. Reputation is tracked per lineage, so clones start at zero and inherit no trust. Attestations are hashed into a ledger as rigid as basalt, so a manufactured swarm cannot rewrite its record, while the real operator stays sealed in a walnut-like shell of signatures.
